title: Split a scored tablet in a pill cutter and put one half in each of two medicine cups
instruction: Split this scored tablet in half with the pill cutter, then put one half in each of the two medicine cups.
context: At home, an older adult or a family carer splits a scored tablet to take half the prescribed dose: it goes in the V of a cheap plastic pill cutter, the lid is pressed down so the blade cuts on the score line, and the halves go into separate cups. Household splitting is a familiar kitchen-table medication-preparation task. The cut is the hard part for a robot: the blade meets the tablet at 12-48 N (5.6-22.2 N at the handle; 14.0 N modelled here), so a light touch stalls instead of cutting.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A typical pill splitter (80 x 40 mm base 11 mm tall with a 20 mm wide V cradle running left-right, fixed to the table by its feet; 30 g in all; its hinged lid (12 g) with a blade over the cradle's middle and a 24 mm tall, 6 mm thick rubber-covered pull fin standing on it near its free edge; the blade's upper 7 mm is inside a 0.6 mm PETG shroud, open only at the cutting edge below the cradle rim) stands at x 0.36, y 0.21 with its hinge on the robot's side. The lid starts open at 95 degrees, past upright, against its stop. One inert 20 x 9 x 7.5 mm scored white tablet (1.8 g; see REAL_TRIAL.md for its source or reproducible surrogate and its 14.0 N batch check) lies in a pill dish at x 0.28, y 0.33, its length left-right. A dosing tray with two 30 mL medicine cups (38 mm inside, 30 mm tall, one orange, one blue, 60 mm apart left-right) stands at x 0.30, y 0.44.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each. (1) The tablet lies in the V cradle at the blade (its middle within 2.5 mm of the blade and the cradle's line, length along the cradle within 8 degrees, level within 8 degrees); once reached. (2) The lid has been shut (within 3 degrees) on it there and the blade's cutting edge, computed from the actual lid pose, has passed the tablet's underside: the cut. (3) The lid is open again, past 80 degrees, as things stand. (4) After the cut, one half is in the orange cup and the other in the blue cup (each inside the cup's wall and below its rim), the cut plane is within 1 mm of the score line, each half's actual mass is 40-60% of the 1.8 g tablet (0.720-1.080 g), and no gripper pad is within 3 cm of either half or of the lid's fin. A 2.5 mm placement offset leaves 7.5 and 12.5 mm halves (0.675/1.125 g), so it fails step 4 and scores 0.6. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once every full-success condition has held together, without a break, for 1 s: all four steps, and the halves within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where they were when that second began; any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8, also while it is being timed. 0 overall if the tablet or a half falls off the table. Closing the lid on an empty cradle or on a badly seated tablet cuts nothing. The sim's blade is a declared cut, but it is force-gated: while the cutting edge is in the tablet (lid 16.5 to 5.5 degrees) the hinge brake is 0.56 N m, 8.24 N at the fin / 14.0 N at the blade at the real 1.7:1 lever, falling to 30% as the score cracks; a weaker push stalls the lid and cuts nothing. The logged force is the hinge drive's reaction at the fin, not the finger pinch.
reset_notes: Open the lid to its 95 degree stop, lay the tablet in the dish pocket with its length left-right, stand the tray on its spot. Between real trials wipe the pad faces, the blade shroud and the V cradle with a 91% IPA wipe and inspect them at 10x for tablet residue (REAL_TRIAL.md); replace the wipe every trial.
fidelity: 240/20 Hz. Sizes: splitter 80x40 mm (95 deg), tablet 20x9x7.5 mm 1.8 g, fin 24x6 mm. Blade 16x0.8x19 mm, edge 7 mm below the lid; the cut is declared when the edge passes the underside; the blade plane leaves 7.5-12.5 mm bodies. A 0.6 mm PETG shroud covers the upper 7 mm; the lower 12 mm is the edge in the V. Hinge brake peaks at 0.56 N m (8.24 N fin, 14.0 N blade), then 30%; logged force is the hinge reaction, not the pinch. Real pad clips are not bodies; the shroud protects the pads.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, completed; 2,401 action rows, model dreamlabs/dream-1-beta, log adhoc_44b767ed.json, top-camera video); demo: 1.0 at step 2045 (Isaac 101.75 s; MuJoCo 102.25 s).
